title: How to align objects with guides in Keynote on Mac: steps for Keynote 15.4
metaTitle: How to Align Objects with Guides in Keynote on Mac
description: How to align objects with guides in Keynote on Mac: turn on guides in Settings, then use the Arrange tab's Align pop-up to line up objects.
targetKeyword: how to align objects with guides in keynote on mac
intro: To align objects with guides in Keynote on Mac, open Keynote > Settings > Rulers and tick the guide types you want. Then select your objects, open the Arrange tab in the Format sidebar, and choose an option from the Align pop-up menu.
tldr: Turn on guides in Keynote > Settings > Rulers, then tick the guide types you need.
Select the objects, open the Arrange tab, and pick an option from the Align pop-up.
Use Distribute for three or more objects, and use View > Guides to hide or clear guides.
Keynote 15.4 needs macOS 26 or later, according to Apple's own note.

blocks.text: Guides and the Align pop-up do two different jobs. Guides are lines that appear while you drag an object, so you can see when an edge or center lines up with something else. The Align pop-up is a one-time command. It moves the objects you selected so they share an edge or a center. Most people use both. Turn on guides to place things by eye, then use Align to tidy the group when you are done.
Check your Keynote version first

This guide follows Keynote 15.4, the version Apple's current Mac user guide covers. To check yours, choose Keynote > About Keynote from the menu bar. Apple says Keynote 15.4 needs macOS 26 or later. Wikipedia lists an older macOS number for the same release, so trust Apple's note on this one.

Keynote for Mac is not the same app as Keynote for iCloud. The iCloud version runs in a browser and has its own settings and menus. Later sections point out where the two differ. If you are on a Mac with the desktop app, the steps here are the ones to follow.
Turn on alignment guides in Keynote settings

Guides are controlled from the settings window, not from the slide. Open Keynote > Settings from the menu bar. Click Rulers in the window that opens. You will see four checkboxes. Each one turns on a different kind of guide.

items: Show guides at object center: a line appears when an object's center lines up with another object.
Show guides at object edges: a line appears when two edges line up.
Show guides for relative sizing: a line appears when an object matches the size of another.
Show guides for relative spacing: a line appears when the gap between objects matches.

blocks.text: Start with center and edges. They cover most layouts. Add sizing and spacing when you build repeated items, such as a row of icons with equal gaps. Next to Alignment Guides, click the color well to change the guide color. Pick a color that shows up on your theme. Close the settings window when you are done.
Align objects with the Align pop-up

Guides help you place things by eye. The Align pop-up sets the position for you. Select the objects, click Arrange at the top of the Format sidebar, then click the Align pop-up menu and choose an option. Apple's pages say to choose an option and do not list each name, so read the menu on your Mac before you pick.

rows: The object farthest in the direction you choose
blocks.caption: Which object Align uses as the reference

blocks.text: The farthest-object rule catches people out. Say you want three text boxes to share a left edge. Keynote treats the box farthest in that direction as the reference. The other boxes move to meet it. If the box you want to keep sits on the right, choose the option for the right side instead.

Run a quick check after each change. Look at the result before you do anything else. If the wrong object moved, press ⌘Z to undo, then try the other direction. It is faster than fixing three objects by hand.
Distribute three or more objects evenly

Distribute spaces objects out. It needs three or more objects, so use Align for a pair. Select the objects, open the Arrange tab, and click the Distribute pop-up menu. Choose Evenly, Horizontally, or Vertically.

Horizontally spaces objects across a row. Vertically spaces them down a column. Evenly is the third choice. Apple's pages do not explain each option in detail, so try it on a copy of your slide to see how it spaces your layout.
Use persistent guides as your own grid

You can also drag guides onto a slide. Turn on rulers first. If the rulers are hidden, click the View button in the toolbar and choose Show Rulers. You can also press ⌘R to show the rulers. Move the pointer over a ruler, then drag onto the slide. Drag a guide to move it.
To remove a guide, drag it off the slide. Drag a horizontal guide up. Drag a vertical guide left. Hand-placed guides stay put while you work, which makes them useful for margins and title positions.
Show, hide, and clear guides from the View menu

The View menu holds the guide controls. Use the menu bar, not the View button in the toolbar. Choose View > Guides > Hide Guides to hide everything. Choose View > Guides > Show Guides to bring them back. Choose View > Guides > Clear All Guides on Slide to remove the guides on the current slide.

Hiding and clearing are not the same. Hiding keeps the guides for later, so you can show them again with one menu choice. Clearing removes them from the slide. Use Hide when you want a clean view for a screenshot or a run-through. Use Clear when the guides are in the way for good.
Keyboard shortcuts for alignment on Mac

Apple's Keynote keyboard shortcut page lists no shortcut for aligning or distributing objects. You will use the Arrange tab for those steps every time. A few shortcuts still help while you place things.

items: Hold ⌘ while you drag an object to turn off alignment guides for that move. The same works while you resize.
⌥⌘G groups the selected objects. ⌥⇧⌘G ungroups them.

blocks.text: Grouping helps with aligned layouts. Once a set of objects lines up, group them, and one drag moves them together. Ungroup them when you need to change one piece. Apple does not list arrow-key nudges for the Mac app. Keynote for iCloud moves a selected object 1 pt per arrow press, and Shift with an arrow moves it 10 pt. Test nudging on your Mac before you rely on it.
A worked example: four logos in one row
Say you have four logos on one slide. They sit at uneven heights and gaps. Turn on the center and edge guides in Keynote > Settings > Rulers. Select all four logos and open the Arrange tab.

Click the Align pop-up and choose the option that lines up the logos on the line you want. Next, keep all four selected and open the Distribute pop-up. Choose Horizontally. The logos now spread across the row. Check the result at a normal zoom level before you call it done.
If one logo still sits a little off, select it alone and test an arrow-key nudge. Keep guides on for the big moves. Turn them off for fine tuning, as the next sections explain.
Mistakes people make with guides and Align

items: Forgetting to select everything. Any object you miss keeps its old position.
Using Distribute on two objects. It needs three or more.
Forgetting the farthest-object rule. The wrong box becomes the reference.
Confusing Hide with Clear. Hide keeps guides for later, and Clear deletes them from the slide.
Following the iCloud menu path on a Mac. Guide settings sit in a different place in the desktop app.
Holding ⌘ and wondering where the guides went. The key turns them off for that one move.

blocks.text: Fix guides that show on every slide

One Apple Community thread from the Keynote 9.1 era describes yellow horizontal lines on every slide. Clear All Guides did not remove them. The suggested fix is View > Edit Master Slides, then View > Guides > Clear All Guides, then View > Exit Master Slides. That thread is old, and the thread does not confirm a fix that worked, so test it on a copy first.

Master slides control what every slide starts with, so a fix there reaches every slide. For more on that layer, read [How to edit the master slide in Keynote on Mac: slide layouts, step by step](/how-to/edit-the-master-slide-in-keynote).
Why objects jump in steps with guides on

One Apple Community post from 2020 says that with alignment guides on, a shape moves in steps of roughly 4 pt. That makes tiny adjustments hard. The poster's workaround is to turn off alignment guides in Rulers settings and set zoom to 400%. This is one user's report, so check it against your own deck.
Use the workaround for fine moves only. Turn guides back on when you are placing objects roughly, because guides save time on most slides.
Keynote for iCloud uses a different path

Keynote for iCloud keeps guides in a different place. Open More in the toolbar, then choose Preferences > Guides. You get three checkboxes: Center guides, Edge guides, and Spacing guides. Apple's iCloud page covers the Arrange tab and the Align pop-up, and those steps match the Mac steps.
Apple's iCloud page does not mention the View menu or Rulers, and it does not compare the two apps. If a Mac step fails in the browser, check whether you are in the iCloud version.
Custom keyboard shortcut for Align Objects

Some people want a key combo for alignment. A user on Apple Community set a custom shortcut for Arrange > Align Objects > Center in System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts > App Shortcuts. Entering the full menu path failed. Entering only the final name, Center, worked for that user.
A combo that another function already uses will not work. That thread is from an older version, so test the shortcut before you rely on it. Pick a combo that no other Keynote command uses.
Where to go next

Once objects line up, the next step is often motion. If your aligned objects need to move in order, read [How to animate an object in Keynote on Mac: step by step for Keynote 15.4](/how-to/animate-an-object-in-keynote). For a whole-deck look, [How to import a theme in Keynote on Mac: a step-by-step guide for Keynote 15.4](/how-to/import-a-theme-in-keynote) covers themes.

faq.question: Why don't I see alignment guides in Keynote on Mac?
faq.answer: Open Keynote > Settings > Rulers and check that at least one of the four Show guides boxes is ticked. Then choose View > Guides > Show Guides, since Apple lists that command for showing guides again. If they still do not appear, check that you are in the Mac app and not Keynote for iCloud.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to align objects in Keynote on Mac?
faq.answer: Apple's keyboard shortcut page lists none for aligning or distributing objects. You can set a custom shortcut in System Settings, but one community report says it works only with the final item name. Hold ⌘ while dragging to turn guides off for a single move.

faq.question: What is the difference between Align and Distribute?
faq.answer: Align lines up the edges or centers of the objects you select. Distribute spaces three or more objects using Evenly, Horizontally, or Vertically. Distribute needs three or more objects, while Align works with two.

faq.question: How do I remove a guide I dragged onto a slide?
faq.answer: Drag it off the slide. Drag a horizontal guide up and a vertical guide left. To remove every guide on the current slide, choose View > Guides > Clear All Guides on Slide.

faq.question: Do the same steps work in Keynote for iCloud?
faq.answer: The Align and Distribute steps follow the same pattern in the web app, under the Arrange tab in the Format sidebar. Guide settings differ, though. Use More > Preferences > Guides in the web app. Apple's iCloud page does not compare the two apps in full, so check each step in your own app.

faq.question: Which macOS do I need for Keynote 15.4?
faq.answer: Apple's What's new page says Keynote 15.4 requires macOS 26 or later. Some third-party pages list a lower macOS number, so check Apple's note before you update. To see your installed version, choose Keynote > About Keynote.

steps.name: Check your Keynote version
steps.text: Open Keynote in the menu bar and choose Keynote > About Keynote. Read the version number in the window. This guide follows Keynote 15.4, which Apple's Mac user guide covers.
steps.tip: If your version is older, expect Preferences where this guide says Settings.

steps.name: Open the guide settings
steps.text: Choose Keynote > Settings. In the settings window, click Rulers. Alignment guides are set here, not on the slide.
steps.tip: Older Apple pages say Preferences instead of Settings. Look for the same Rulers section.

steps.name: Tick the guide types you want
steps.text: Check Show guides at object center, Show guides at object edges, Show guides for relative sizing, or Show guides for relative spacing. Click the color well next to Alignment Guides if you want a different guide color.
steps.tip: Start with center and edges. Add sizing and spacing when you need them.

steps.name: Select the objects
steps.text: Click the first object, then add the others to the selection. Select at least two objects. Select three or more if you plan to distribute them.
steps.tip: Any object you miss keeps its old position, so check the selection before you align.

steps.name: Open the Arrange tab
steps.text: Click Arrange at the top of the Format sidebar. If the sidebar is hidden, the Arrange controls open in a separate window from View > Show Arrange Tools.
steps.tip: Keep the objects selected while you switch to the Arrange tab.

steps.name: Choose an option from the Align pop-up
steps.text: Click the Align pop-up menu and choose the option that matches the edge or center you want. One selected object aligns to the slide. Several selected objects align to the one farthest in the direction you chose.
steps.tip: Apple's pages say choose an option without naming each one. Read the list on your Mac before you choose.

steps.name: Distribute three or more objects
steps.text: Select three or more objects. In the Arrange tab, click the Distribute pop-up menu. Choose Evenly, Horizontally, or Vertically.
steps.tip: Distribute needs three or more objects, so use Align for a pair.

steps.name: Hide, show, or clear guides
steps.text: Choose View > Guides, then pick Hide Guides, Show Guides, or Clear All Guides on Slide. Use the menu bar for these, not the View button in the toolbar.
steps.tip: Clear All Guides on Slide removes the guides you placed. Hide keeps them for later.

steps.name: Move without guides
steps.text: Hold ⌘ while you drag or resize an object to turn off alignment guides for that move.
steps.tip: Let go of ⌘ and the guides come back for the next move.

troubleshooting.problem: Guide lines appear on every slide
troubleshooting.fix: Try View > Edit Master Slides, then View > Guides > Clear All Guides, then View > Exit Master Slides. One older thread reports this fix, so save a copy of the deck first.

troubleshooting.problem: Clear All Guides does not remove the lines
troubleshooting.fix: The same older thread says the master slide route can clear them. It does not confirm the fix worked for everyone, so test it on a copy.

troubleshooting.problem: Guides do not show up at all
troubleshooting.fix: Recheck the four Show guides boxes in Keynote > Settings > Rulers. Then choose View > Guides > Show Guides, which Apple lists for showing them again.

troubleshooting.problem: Objects move in steps of about 4 pt
troubleshooting.fix: One 2020 community user reported this with guides on. Turn guides off in Rulers settings, set zoom to 400%, and make the fine move. Turn guides back on afterward.

troubleshooting.problem: Align option names differ from this guide
troubleshooting.fix: Apple's pages do not list each option name. Read the Align menu on your Mac, pick the edge or center you need, and check About Keynote if a choice is missing.

troubleshooting.problem: A custom shortcut for Align does nothing
troubleshooting.fix: Enter only the final item name, Center, as one community user did. Pick a combo that no other function uses, because a taken combo will not work.
